mutation_targets.rationale: F_AuthRequired is the only fact directly forbidding a successful op with no caller (F_CallerIsTokenResolved is intentionally weakened to fire only when a caller exists). Removing it and forcing such an op makes the auth-required invariant fail.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthRequiredViolation { some op: Operation | op.outcome = Success and no op.caller and op.role = MemberRole }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_LeastPrivilege is the only fact tying Operation success to a matrix cell. Clearing it and forcing a successful Anonymous-role op produces an instance where (role -> kind) is not in PermMatrix.Allowed, which the LeastPrivilege predicate must reject.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.outcome = Success and op.role = Anonymous and some op.caller and op.kind = ViewTask }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_DeletionLogCompleteness is the only fact requiring every successful delete to spawn a log entry. Clearing it and injecting a successful delete with no log directly contradicts the completeness predicate.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some op: Operation | op.kind = DeleteTask and op.outcome = Success and no op.deletionLog and some op.targetTask and some op.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_DeletionLogAttribution is the only fact aligning a log entry's deleter/taskRef with the operation's caller/targetTask. Clearing it lets a delete op record a deleter different from its caller, which the AttributionCorrectness predicate explicitly rejects.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some op: Operation | some op.deletionLog and op.deletionLog.deleter != op.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_AppendOnlyDeletionLog is the only fact enforcing a 1-to-1 mapping between log entries and successful delete operations. Removing it and forcing two distinct operations to share a single DeletionLogEntry constructs an instance the AppendOnly predicate must flag.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj op1, op2: Operation | some op1.deletionLog and op1.deletionLog = op2.deletionLog }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_ClosedTaskEditRule is the only fact blocking a successful edit of a Done task that doesn't transition it out of Done. Clearing it and injecting such an edit (preStatus = newStatus = Done with outcome Success) violates the closed-task edit predicate directly.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ClosedTaskEditViolation { some op: Operation | op.kind = EditTask and op.outcome = Success and op.preStatus = Done and op.newStatus = Done and some op.targetTask and some op.caller }
